newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees 75 pct scripless share trading by June.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees 75 pct scripless share trading by June.

text.p: The president of the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) said on Thursday he wants 75 percent of the exchange's trading volume to be scripless by June.

"I want to get 75 percent of the daily volumes scripless by June. If we can get volumes from institutional fund managers scripless, then that's already something," PSE president Vitaliano Nanagas II told Reuters after a ceremony marking the registration of the first share for scripless trading.
Shares of the firm, Jollibee Foods Corp, will be kept at the Philippine Central Depository Inc and any trades in the counter will be backed by confirmation receipts.
Nanagas said that other issues which will soon go scripless are Ayala Land, Fil-Estate Land Inc and Metropolitan Bank & Trust.

"We are not planning to go scripless 100 percent because the issue is not to get 100 percent but to get it available to those who want. There is also the capacity constraint where we can only convert so many shares at a time," Nanagas added.
He said scripless trading will boost volume turnover at the bourse as settlement of trades will be shortened.

"I will be happy to see a 20 percent increase in volumes. All I know is that people are not looking at us because we are not scripless and now that we are, they will be forced to take a look." - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418939
